rfi.title: Hundreds detained after violent clashes on PSG victory night

rfi.title: Last hurrah: Brazil's Neymar
rfi.description: Neymar will play for Brazil at the World Cup for the fourth time at the age of 34. In the third of a series on players at their final World Cup, RFI looks back at the career of a striker who holds his country's record for both scoring and assisting goals.

lemonde.description: « Dans ma bulle. » L’autrice de bande dessinée fait partie des artistes à l’honneur de l’exposition « LGBTQomics », à Angoulême. Elle lance, avec la maison d’édition qu’elle a fondée, une collection consacrée à la romance queer.

france24fr.title: Au Danemark, la Première ministre sortante Mette Frederiksen a constitué un gouvernement
france24fr.description: Mette Frederiksen va présenter cette semaine sa nouvelle équipe, après avoir annoncé lundi soir avoir réussi à constituer une coalition gouvernementale de gauche. La Première ministre danoise était sortie affaiblie des élections législatives du 24 mars, puisque le parti social-démocrate qu'elle dirige avait réalisé son plus mauvais résultat depuis 1903.

france24fr.title: Une attaque du groupe jihadiste ADF tue 16 personnes à Beni dans l'est de la RD Congo
france24fr.description: Dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo, les jihadistes ADF, affilié à l’État islamique, ont mené une attaque dans la ville de Beni. C’est la première fois depuis plus de trois ans que les ADF frappent à l’intérieur de la ville, un signe préoccupant.

france24fr.title: Sénégal : Ousmane Sonko annonce que le Pastef ne participera pas au nouveau gouvernement
Sénégal : le Pastef d'Ousmane Sonko ne participera pas au nouveau gouvernement
france24fr.description: Le Pastef, le parti d'Ousmane Sonko, ne participera pas au nouveau gouvernement du président Bassirou Diomaye Faye, a annoncé, lundi, l'ancien Premier ministre limogé fin mai.

france24fr.title: Iran : le président Massoud Pezeshkian sur le départ ?
france24fr.description: Alors qu’un accord de cessez-le-feu semble s’éloigner de plus en plus entre l’Iran et les Etats-Unis, des rumeurs ont circulé quant à une démission du président iranien Massoud Pezeshkian.

france24fr.title: Roland-Garros : fin du rêve pour Parry, Auger-Aliassime pour la première fois en quarts
france24fr.description: Les affiches des quarts de finale de Roland-Garros sont quasiment bouclées et elles ne compteront aucun Français : dernière survivante d'une semaine caniculaire, Diane Parry s'est arrêtée lundi. Le Canadien Félix-Auger Aliassime, lui, en revanche, peut continuer de rêver.

france24fr.title: Un hommage national sera rendu à Edgar Morin mercredi aux Invalides
france24fr.description: Emmanuel Macron présidera, mercredi aux Invalides, un hommage national au sociologue et philosophe Edgar Morin, décédé le 29 mai à l'âge de 104 ans.

france24fr.title: France: l'atout nucléaire pour attirer les data centers
france24fr.description: Au sommet Choose France, des investissements records ont été annoncés et notamment dans la construction de data centers. La France attire ce secteur très énergivore grâce à ses capacités de production d'électricité basées sur le nucléaire. Pour l'instant, elle produit beaucoup plus d'électricité qu'elle n'en consomme mais certains craignent que l'appétit de l'IA force la France à faire des choix au détriment de sa transition énergétique.

france24fr.title: Israël/Liban : un tournant dans le sud ?
france24fr.description: L'armée israélienne a appelé les habitants de la banlieue sud de Beyrouth à évacuer les lieux en prévision de frappes contre le Hezbollah. Cet ordre intervient après une intensification des hostilités dans le sud du Liban au cours du week-end, marquée par la prise de la forteresse médiévale stratégique de Beaufort par les troupes israéliennes. L'ONU s'est dite "très inquiète" et a appelé, ce lundi, toutes les parties à respecter le cessez-le-feu et à éviter une "nouvelle escalade".

france24fr.title: En direct : Trump affirme qu'Israël a accepté de ne pas envoyer de troupes à Beyrouth
Madagascar : quatre juges de la Haute Cour constitutionnelle dans le viseur de la justice
france24fr.description: À Madagascar, des magistrats se retrouvent dans le viseur de la justice. Le parquet d'Antananarivo souhaite engager des poursuites contre quatre juges de la Haute Cour constitutionnelle accusés de complot en vue de déstabilisation. Une procédure qui intervient après que cette même cour a jugé irrecevable une requête en destitution du président malgache.

france24fr.title: Pourquoi la propagandiste russe Xenia Fedorova embarrasse-t-elle l’exécutif français ?
france24fr.description: Chroniqueuse dans les médias de la galaxie Bolloré au service de la propagande russe, Xenia Fedorova embarrasse désormais l’exécutif à double titre : le ministre de l’Intérieur a dû expliquer pourquoi son titre de séjour avait été renouvelé pour dix ans en 2024, tandis que la ministre de l’Agriculture a participé à un déjeuner en sa compagnie.

france24fr.title: La France et la Russie à couteaux tirés ?
france24fr.description: La marine de Brest a arraisonné hier le "Tagor", un pétrolier sous sanctions européennes en provenance de Russie. Il s'agit du quatrième pétrolier de la flotte fantôme, utilisée par Moscou pour contourner les sanctions, à être intercepté par la France depuis septembre. Les explications avec Nicolas Tenzer, politologue, enseignant à Sciences Po, spécialiste des questions stratégiques et internationales.

france24fr.title: Malte : explosion dans une usine de feux d'artifice
france24fr.description: Une puissante explosion au sein d'une fabrique de feux d'artifice lundi à Malte a fait deux blessés, et projeté dans les airs des débris et un panache de fumée imposant, a indiqué la police.

france24fr.title: La France interdit les armes offensives israéliennes au salon Eurosatory
france24fr.description: Sur décision du gouvernement français, lundi, seuls les exposants israéliens présentant des systèmes de défense antibalistique et antiaérienne seront autorisés à l'occasion du salon Eurosatory, près de Paris, prévu du 15 au 19 juin.

france24fr.title: "TechXit" : pourquoi Peter Thiel mise sur l’Argentine de Javier Milei
france24fr.description: Le controversé patron de Palantir, Peter Thiel, va temporairement élire domicile en Argentine, ont appris plusieurs médias. Pour ce libertarien de droite autoproclamé, l’expérience économique radicale de Javier Milei convient davantage que le modèle trumpien aux États-Unis. Un déménagement qui en dit long, aussi, sur les priorités de ces barons de la tech.

france24fr.title: Au Liban, la forteresse de Beaufort, un lieu symbolique des conflits dans la région
france24fr.description: L'armée israélienne a annoncé dimanche s'être emparée de la forteresse de Beaufort dans le cadre de l'intensification de son offensive dans le Sud-Liban. Ce château est le symbole des guerres qui ont marqué la région, des croisades du Moyen Âge aux occupations israéliennes.

france24fr.title: Kenya, huit élèves interpellés après l’incendie d’un pensionnat
france24fr.description: Au Kenya, huit filles ont été arrêtées, soupçonnées d'être impliquées dans l'incendie dévastateur d’un pensionnat. Au moins seize étudiantes ont été tuées dans l'incendie qui a ravagé un dortoir de l’Utumishi Girls Academy. Les familles attendent toujours l'identification de certaines des victimes.

nzz.description: Erst das Dementi, dann das Ausweichen, nun die Bestätigung: Der Superstar will kommende Woche auf die Tour zurückkehren – im Alter von 44 Jahren.

nzz.title: ERKLÄRT - Reisende aufgepasst: Italien erstattet bei langen Baustellenstaus die Maut
nzz.description: Sobald die Sommerferien starten, rollt in Italien die grosse Reisewelle an. Happige Mautgebühren gehören auf den Autobahnen ebenso dazu wie lange Staus. Doch bei Verzögerungen infolge von Baustellen gibt es nun einfacher Geld zurück. Antworten auf die wichtigsten Fragen.

spiegel.title: Belgien: Belgische Fahnder entdecken neue Fährte nach Juwelendiebstahl im Louvre
spiegel.description: In Belgien haben Ermittler auf Handys verdächtige Fotos aus dem Saal im Louvre gefunden, in dem sich die gestohlenen Kronjuwelen befanden. Nun soll geprüft werden, ob es eine Verbindung zu den vier inhaftierten Tatverdächtigen gibt.

spiegel.title: Iran-Krieg: Donald Trump spricht von Fortsetzung der Iran-Gespräche – und Deeskalation zwischen Israel und Hisbollah
spiegel.description: Donald Trump widerspricht Berichten, Iran würde die Verhandlungen mit den USA abbrechen. Zudem habe Israels Premier Netanyahu dem US-Präsidenten in einem Telefonat zugesichert, keine Truppen nach Beirut zu schicken.

spiegel.title: Kevin Keegan: Krebserkrankung von Englands Fußball-Ikone im fortgeschrittenen Stadium
spiegel.description: Nach einem Autounfall entdeckten Ärzte bei Kevin Keegan Krebs: Davon berichtet der frühere englische Nationalcoach und HSV-Star nun. Inzwischen sei die Erkrankung im fortgeschrittenen Stadium.

spiegel.title: Harvard-Universität: Kam ein Nazi in die USA. Und wurde in Ehren empfangen
spiegel.description: Die Harvard-Universität gilt als Eldorado der Wissenschaftsfreiheit. Die ganze Wahrheit ist das nicht. Denn immer wieder beugte sich die Institution den Mächtigen.

spiegel.title: ChatGPT-Konkurrent Anthropic meldet Börsengang an
spiegel.description: Der Entwickler des Chatbots Claude will an die Börse. Zuletzt wurde das US-Unternehmen mit 965 Milliarden Dollar bewertet. Die Konkurrenz hegt ähnliche Pläne.

spiegel.title: FDP: Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann will überraschende Kandidatur erst zwei Tage vor Parteitag beschlossen haben
spiegel.description: Spontane Aktion oder länger geplanter Angriff? Mit ihrer kurzfristigen Bewerbung um den FDP-Vorsitz hatte Marie-Agnes Strack-Zimmermann Teile der Partei in Schockstarre versetzt. Nun gibt sie Einblicke in die Planung des Wahldramas.

spiegel.title: Netflix, Amazon Prime, Disney+: Neue Filme und Serien im Juni 2026
spiegel.description: Polen kann queere Serien, Nicolas Cage kann schauspielern und ARD-Serien können witzig sein: Was im Juni anläuft und welche Klassiker einen zweiten Blick verdient haben.

spiegel.title: Fußball-WM 2026: Neymar, Ronaldo, Messi – und ein Oberliga-Kicker aus Koblenz
spiegel.description: Diese WM wird ein besonderes Turnier, und das liegt nicht nur am Haupt-Gastgeber USA und an der aufgestockten Teilnehmerzahl. Ein Blick auf die Kader verrät: Es wird die Weltmeisterschaft der alten Männer.

spiegel.title: Bafög: Warum Studierende jetzt doch um die Erhöhung bangen müssen
spiegel.description: Der Koalitionsstreit ums Bafög war beigelegt, die Finanzierung der Erhöhung geklärt. Doch nun stellt die Union den Plan wieder infrage und erzürnt die SPD. Was das für Studierende bedeutet – der Überblick.

spiegel.title: FDP und die Brandmauer zur AfD: Was hinter dem neuen Kurs von Wolfgang Kubicki steckt
spiegel.description: Unter ihrem neuen Parteichef Wolfgang Kubicki sagt sich die FDP von der Brandmauer zur AfD los. Der Politikwissenschaftler Thomas Biebricher sagt, warum die Partei diesen Schritt geht und welche Gefahren das birgt.

spiegel.title: Cenk Uygur und Hasan Piker: Großbritannien verweigert politischen Streamern Einreise wegen Aussagen zu Israel
spiegel.description: Den US-Publizisten Hasan Piker und Cenk Uygur wird in Israel Antisemitismus vorgeworfen. Bei einer Konferenz in Großbritannien sollten beide als Redner auftreten, die Einreise wurden ihnen jetzt verweigert.

spiegel.title: Rauchen und Nichtraucherschutzgesetz: In welchen Bundesländern welche Regeln gelten
spiegel.description: In Baden-Württemberg darf in Freibädern nicht mehr geraucht werden, Bremen plant ebenfalls strengere Vorschriften. Auch sonst gilt: Wer eine Landesgrenze überschreitet, muss sich oft an neue Regeln halten. Der Überblick.

spiegel.title: Charli xcx: Martin Scorsese, John Cale und Marc Jacobs auf dem Cover von »'Music, Fashion, Film«
spiegel.description: Der »Brat«-Sommer ist vorbei, huldigt Charli xcx jetzt alten Männern? Den Gedanken legt das Cover zum Album »Music, Fashion, Film« nahe, das die Musikerin jetzt vorab veröffentlichte.

spiegel.title: »Stiftung Flucht, Vertreibung, Versöhnung«: Über 500.000 Euro verschwunden - Untreueverdacht
spiegel.description: Erst gab es politische Querelen, jetzt droht der »Stiftung Flucht, Vertreibung, Versöhnung« eine Finanzaffäre: Nach SPIEGEL-Informationen sollen mehr als 500.000 Euro veruntreut worden sein – unter anderem für Luxusuhren und Goldbarren.

spiegel.title: Elektroauto kaufen gebraucht: Fahrer in Deutschland stürmen Markt für E-Pkw
spiegel.description: Die Nachfrage nach gebrauchten Elektroautos in Deutschland wächst stark – das hat offenbar mit dem Irankrieg zu tun. In der Statistik eines großen Verkaufsportals zeigen sich einschneidende Folgen.

observador.title: Pinto Luz avisa futuros governos sobre construção
observador.description: Na apresentação da Fundação da Construção, o ministro das Infraestruturas pediu também aos próximos governos que não descartem o que foi feito. O setor vale 5% do PIB.

observador.title: Banana artistica roubada por visitante do Pompidou-Metz
observador.description: Não foram  verificados "danos irreversíveis" e banana já foi substituída. Centro de exposições francês afirma que apresentou queixa às autoridades "contra pessoas desconhecidas".

observador.title: Rússia acusa França de serem os novos piratas do mar
observador.description: Rússia acusa França de pirataria. Depois da marinha francesa ter interceptado um petroleiro russo com bens sancionados, pela UE e UK. Ainda, Kremlin acusa Ucrânia de "irresponsabilidade nuclear".

observador.title: Netanyahu ameaça Beirute e mantém ataques no sul do Líbano
observador.description: O primeiro-ministro israelita comunicou a Trump que manterá os bombardeamentos a Beirute e as operações no sul do Líbano, horas após os EUA anunciarem um acordo com o Hezbollah.

observador.title: Transparência salarial. O que pode mudar nas empresas?
observador.description: Diretiva europeia proíbe perguntas sobre histórico salarial e impõe auditorias para identificar desigualdades de género. Portugal devia transpô-la até ao próximo domingo mas ainda não o fez.

observador.title: Ébola. 263 casos e 43 mortes confirmadas na RDCongo e Uganda
observador.description: "Ministério da Saúde, a OMS e parceiros estão a trabalhar para realizar ensaios controlados sobre vacinas e tratamentos", afirma a OMS na sequência da visita do diretor-geral a Bunia.

observador.title: Ucrânia tem janela limitada para negociar com a Rússia
observador.description: Em entrevista à CBS News, Zelensky afirma que a Ucrânia está na melhor altura possível, para pressionar a Rússia a ir à mesa de negociações. Acredita que a Rússia está à beira de uma crise política

observador.title: As notícias das 22h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: Pacto europeu de asilo implica reformas
observador.description: Novo pacto visa harmonizar regras e procedimentos de migrações e asilo no espaço comunitário. Entra em vigor dia 12 junho, mas Manuel Jarmela alerta para as reformas organizacionais necessárias.

observador.title: Cascais. Acidente entre autocarro e carro faz um morto
observador.description: Um morto e dois feridos leves foi o resultado de um choque entre um autocarro e um automóvel em Cascais. O acidente condicionou o trânsito durante mais de três horas.

observador.title: “A minha mulher e o meu filho estavam sob ataque no Irão”
observador.description: Apostado em fazer do mundo um lugar melhor, projeto a projeto, Pedro Queirós, aventureiro humanitário, cumpre sonhos impossíveis como correr 100 maratonas em 100 dias.

observador.title: "Mas tu não pensas?!" Já disse isto ao seu filho?
observador.description: Há palavras que ferem mais do que outras. E há períodos na vida, sobretudo até aos 12 anos, em que as palavras podem ter um efeito muito negativo no crescimento.

observador.title: As marcas que movem Portugal
observador.description: Ao longo das últimas décadas, o Grupo Brisa criou marcas que transformaram a mobilidade dos portugueses. Com Hugo Bento, Diretor de Marketing da Brisa, falamos de comunicação, proximidade e inovação.

observador.title: O futuro da indústria depende do bem-estar das pessoas
observador.description: Para Victor Rodrigues, administrador da Elior e Derichebourg Facility Services, uma indústria forte só pode ser construída com equipas valorizadas, preparadas e motivadas.

observador.title: 21h. Paulo Carmona eleito presidente da IP
observador.description: Paulo Carmona era até agora diretor geral da Direção Geral de Energia e Geologia. Ainda, o Ministério Público investiga a morte de mais seis vitimas da tempestade Kristin.

observador.title: O 3.º reforço para o meio-campo: Sporting anuncia Doumbia
observador.description: Depois de Rodrigo Zalazar e Pedro Lima, os leões mantêm-se muito ativos no mercado e confirmaram a contratação de Issa Doumbia, médio de 22 anos que estava no Venezia e custou 20 milhões de euros.

observador.title: Líder do PCP pede adesão à greve geral
observador.description: O dirigente do PCP afirmou que a contestação à lei laboral não vai terminar com a paralisação de quarta-feira, prevendo a continuação da luta contra o que considerou ser um retrocesso nos direitos.

observador.title: Sindicatos da PSP lamentam acordo parado com Governo
observador.description: O acordo assinado em julho de 2024 entre a PSP e o Governo, para começar a negociar a tabela remuneratória, os suplementos e o estatuto profissional, continua por concretizar.

elpais.title: Trump intenta rescatar el preacuerdo con Irán y asegura que Israel frenará su ofensiva en Líbano
elpais.description: Netanyahu subraya que su ejército “seguirá actuando en el sur de Líbano como estaba planeado” y atacará también Beirut si Hezbolá sigue disparando contra las localidades del norte de Israel

elpais.title: La guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, en directo | Netanyahu responde a Trump y anuncia que su ejército actuará en el sur de Líbano “como estaba planeado”
elpais.description: El republicano afirma que ha frenado una operación israelí en Beirut después de que Irán suspendiese las negociaciones | Líbano asegura que Hezbolá y Estados Unidos han acordado detener sus ataques cruzados

elpais.title: Feijóo ofrece a PNV y Junts un Gobierno sin Vox para ir a las urnas: “Hay 184 diputados que pedimos elecciones”
elpais.description: El líder del PP plantea un Ejecutivo popular que “limpiaría las instituciones”, entre ellas RTVE, para convocar después los comicios. Fuentes del PNV se remiten a las palabras de Aitor Esteban, quien ha descartado apoyar una moción

elpais.title: Los primeros testigos dejan tocadas varias de las acusaciones contra el hermano del Sánchez
elpais.description: El autor del correo en el que se aludía al “hermanísimo” admite que era un “rumor” y varios funcionarios defienden la legalidad del proceso

elpais.title: La profesora agredida en Valencia presenta una denuncia y la Policía Nacional abre expediente al agente que la empujó
elpais.description: El suceso se produjo en una concentración durante la negociación este domingo entre la Generalitat y los sindicatos para desconvocar la huelga indefinida en marcha desde el 11 de mayo

elpais.title: La corriente del Pisuerga alejó a la madre y la abuela que murieron ahogadas en Palencia intentando rescatar a un niño de cinco años
elpais.description: El menor estaba jugando con una tabla de surf infantil cuando el río lo separó de la orilla y sus familiares se lanzaron a salvarlo

elpais.title: “¡Queremos gordas!”: la Casita de Bad Bunny y la polémica por la selección de mujeres normativas para llenarla
elpais.description: Un grupo de ojeadores recluta entre el público a chicas para que compartan escenario con el cantante y un grupo de famosos

elpais.title: Iván Cepeda: “No hay irregularidades de dimensiones suficientes para hablar de fraude”
elpais.description: El candidato presidencial del oficialismo reconoce los resultados de las elecciones del domingo, sobre las que el presidente Gustavo Petro había puesto un manto de duda ante un supuesto fraude

elpais.title: Abelardo de la Espriella, tras su victoria en Colombia y los cuestionamientos de Petro: “Defenderemos la democracia por la razón o por la fuerza”
elpais.description: El candidato de ultraderecha censura la decisión del presidente de desconocer el preconteo. “El pueblo se va a levantar”, advierte

elpais.title: De la Espriella y Cepeda se disputarán la presidencia de Colombia mientras Petro cuestiona los resultados
elpais.description: El candidato ultra logra el 43,7% de los votos y el aspirante de izquierda, un 40,9%. El presidente duda del sistema de preconteo y rechaza los datos publicados este domingo

elpais.title: Siete claves de las elecciones en Colombia: el auge ultra, la unidad de la izquierda y la importancia de los votos del centro
elpais.description: La segunda vuelta entre De la Espriella e Iván Cepeda marcará un escenario inédito

elpais.title: La UE reafirma el endurecimiento de su política migratoria al validar la creación de centros de deportación en terceros países
elpais.description: El Consejo y el Parlamento Europeo acuerdan los términos del nuevo reglamento de retornos que allana el camino para enviar a los migrantes rechazados a terceros países fuera de la UE, incluidas familias con menores

elpais.title: Trump da marcha atrás al fondo de 1.776 millones para compensar a sus aliados “perseguidos” por Biden
elpais.description: El Departamento de Justicia anuncia que acata la sentencia que tumba la creación de esa reserva de dinero. La medida abría la puerta a una indemnización de los atacantes del Capitolio

elpais.title: Sheinbaum evita incluir a Trump en sus críticas injerencistas a Estados Unidos: “No creo que sea quien encabeza esta ofensiva”
elpais.description: La presidenta de México afirma que no es el líder republicano quien alienta la injerencia en México, sino sectores de ultraderecha

elpais.title: Frederiksen alcanza un acuerdo de gobierno en Dinamarca para un tercer mandato
elpais.description: La socialdemócrata, en el poder desde 2019, liderará un Ejecutivo de coalición con un partido centrista y otros dos de izquierdas

elpais.title: Un Bluetooth con el nombre “bomba” obliga a dar la vuelta a un vuelo de Estados Unidos a España
elpais.description: La tripulación del United Airlines destino a Palma de Mallorca pidió a los 190 pasajeros que apagaran sus dispositivos pero dos de ellos permanecían encendidos. El piloto decidió volver a Newark e inspeccionar el Boeing 767

elpais.title: Anthropic se adelanta a OpenAI y registra la solicitud para su multimillonaria salida a Bolsa
elpais.description: La empresa dirigida por Dario Amodei presenta la documentación ante el supervisor bursátil para comenzar a cotizar el próximo otoño

elpais.title: Begoña Gómez acusa a Peinado de actuar con “una velocidad de crucero incompatible” con un Estado democrático
elpais.description: Su abogado presenta un recurso contra la decisión del juez de citarle a comparecer el 9 de junio para abordar la procedencia de la apertura del juicio oral

nyt.title: Losing Trust in Justice Dept., Judges Call Out Its Lawyers’ Behavior
nyt.description: The federal courts have long assumed that the government’s lawyers are trustworthy. Now judges across the country are criticizing their lack of candor.

nyt.title: Oil Prices Jump as Middle East Tensions Build
nyt.description: Some analysts said the main international oil price, which was up 6 percent on Monday, could climb much higher in the coming weeks if the Strait of Hormuz doesn’t reopen.

nyt.title: Anthropic Files to Go Public, Setting Stage for Huge I.P.O.
nyt.description: The artificial intelligence company, which is racing OpenAI to the stock market, has seen explosive growth over the last year thanks largely to technology that can automatically write computer code.

nyt.title: California’s Public Universities Went All in on A.I. Now They’re Tearing Themselves Apart.
nyt.description: California’s public universities spent $16.9 million on A.I. during a financial crisis, and the result has been chaos.

nyt.title: How Box Created 13 New Types of Jobs Because of A.I.
nyt.description: Box, a Silicon Valley software maker, expects to have more employees, not fewer, as it hires A.I. architects, A.I. solutions managers and other new A.I.-related positions.

nyt.title: Is A.I. Replacing Tech Workers or Providing an Excuse for Job Cuts?
nyt.description: Tech industry layoffs are accelerating, and executives have been quick to say it’s because their companies are doing more with artificial intelligence, even when there may be more to it.

nyt.title: Scott Pelley Accuses CBS News Boss of ‘Murdering’ ‘60 Minutes’
nyt.description: In an explosive staff meeting, Mr. Pelley, a correspondent for the long-running Sunday news show, blasted Bari Weiss, the CBS editor in chief, and Nick Bilton, the show’s new executive producer.

nyt.title: The Return of Blaming and Shaming in Public Health
nyt.description: For years, medicine has tried to eliminate stigma. Now, Robert F. Kennedy Jr. is bringing back the language of personal responsibility.

nyt.title: Mills Reminds Maine Voters She’s ‘Still on the Ballot’ for Senate Amid Platner Controversy
nyt.description: A month after withdrawing from the state’s Senate race, Gov. Janet Mills suggested she remained an option after the likely Democratic nominee, Graham Platner, faced a new scandal.

nyt.title: Inside the NYC Primary Between Antonio Reynoso and Claire Valdez
nyt.description: The Democratic battle over a House seat in New York City has reignited old tensions over gentrification, identity and who gets to define the left.

nyt.title: Alberta’s Movement to Separate from Canada Gets Its Moment
nyt.description: In October, Albertans will get to say if they want to stay in Canada, or hold a referendum to leave. Will it settle the matter, or deepen the rift?

nyt.title: Alberta Will Vote on a Possible Referendum to Separate From Canada. Here’s What to Know.
nyt.description: Premier Danielle Smith announced that she would ask citizens to vote on whether they want to stay in Canada, or hold a referendum to secede.

nyt.title: Joana Avillez Revisits Her Waterfront Childhood
nyt.description: Joana Avillez took six years to illustrate a new edition of Joseph Mitchell’s “The Bottom of the Harbor,” which captures the salty New York neighborhood of her youth.

nyt.title: Marilyn Monroe Fans Descended on Palm Springs For Her 100th Birthday
nyt.description: To honor her centennial, over 1,000 Marilyn Monroe fans came together to dress as the screen legend in Palm Springs, where her Hollywood career began.

nyt.title: Marco Rubio: Florida Centrist, Tea Party Darling, MAGA Warrior, President?
nyt.description: The secret to the secretary of state’s success.

nyt.title: Why This Summer Travel Season Will Be a Nightmare
nyt.description: Air travel could be disrupted into next year because of high jet fuel prices.

nyt.title: Giant Stone Urns Hint at the Death Rites of a Lost People in Laos
nyt.description: Thousands of mysterious containers lie scattered across northern Laos. These “death jars” may have provided a form of communal interment, archaeologists reported.

npr.title: Iran halts talks with U.S. over Israeli actions in Lebanon, Gaza
npr.description: Trumps says Israel and Hezbollah will stop fighting after Iran stops talks with U.S. over Israeli operations in southern Lebanon, Gaza

npr.title: U.S. strikes Iranian military sites. And, Trump's $1.8 billion fund faces scrutiny
npr.description: American aircraft fired on a number of Iranian sites over the weekend, including Qeeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. And, Trump's anti-weaponization fund faces scrutiny in Congress and the courts.

npr.title: Confirmed Ebola cases in Congo near 300 as survivors describe their recoveries
npr.description: The outbreak remains focused in Congo's eastern Ituri province. Congo has reported over 1,000 suspected cases with the Bundibugyo virus, which has no approved treatment or vaccine.

npr.title: Funds for Trump's Board of Peace aren't in World Bank account. So where are they?
npr.description: NPR's Steve Inskeep speaks with Financial Times reporter Abigail Hauslohner about the funding of President Trump's Board of Peace to oversee Gaza's reconstruction.

npr.title: After Russian missile strike, owners of Ukrainian coffee shop pledge to rebuild
npr.description: After a large-scale Russian missile strike hit downtown Kyiv, the owners of a coffee shop that opened just hours earlier were already serving coffee again and planning to rebuild.

npr.title: Violent clashes give way to peaceful PSG parade after Champions League win
npr.description: A huge crowd of supporters gathered peacefully near the Eiffel Tower on Sunday to celebrate Paris Saint-Germain's victory, which was marred by violent clashes overnight that led police to detain hundreds of people.

npr.title: Right-wing candidate pulls ahead in first round of Colombia's presidential vote
npr.description: Tough-on-crime outsider Aberaldo de la Espriella took the lead in Colombia's presidential race on Sunday night, setting up a runoff with Iván Cepeda, an ally of outgoing President Gustavo Petro.

npr.title: U.S. bombs Iranian military sites, then downs missiles Tehran fired at troops in Kuwait
npr.description: The U.S. says it has bombed radar and drone sites in Iran after Tehran shot down an American drone over the weekend. Iran then said it targeted American soldiers in Kuwait with missiles, which the U.S. says it shot down on Monday.

npr.title: How aid cuts are hampering the front-line response to the Ebola crisis
npr.description: Aid workers in Uganda are watching an Ebola crisis unfold in neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo. They're doing what they can to prepare for an uptick in cases, but foreign aid cuts aren't helping.

npr.title: The terrifying day the U.S.-Iran war reached a sleepy Sri Lankan town
npr.description: A deadly strike during the first days of the Iran war hit far away in the Indian Ocean, jolting a quiet seaside town and showing how far the conflict's reach extends.

republika.title: Rihanna recluta la figlia di Musk per la campagna del suo brand
republika.description: Ripudiato il padre Vivian è ora protagonista della campagna fotografica Savage x Fenty della pop star che rivendica l’orgoglio Lgbtq+. Lui aveva accusato la sinistra di averle fatto il lavaggio del cervello

republika.title: Patto di stabilità, l’Ue apre all’Italia: flessibilità sull’energia ma non per i sussidi
republika.description: Le spese per gli investimenti necessari a fronteggiare il caro-energia non sarebbero considerate per il calcolo del deficit, come accade per la difesa

republika.description: Zelensky: “Mosca rapisce i nostri bambini, ho le prove”

republika.title: Ragazzo scomparso nelle acque del Ticino a Vigevano: ricerche con sommozzatori, elicottero e droni
republika.description: Il giovane, 23 anni, si è tuffato nel tratto di fiume vicino al cantiere del nuovo ponte

republika.title: A 17 anni scompare nel Chisone davanti agli amici “Forse voleva recuperare una ciabatta in acqua”
republika.description: A Porte, nel Torinese, le ricerche disperate dei vigili del fuoco per un ragazzo caduto nel torrente e portato via dalla corrente

republika.title: Mattarella condanna le bombe: “Medio Oriente nel caos, basta prepotenza delle armi”
republika.description: Il discorso del capo dello Stato che ha ricevuto al Quirinale il corpo diplomatico accreditato in Italia alla vigilia del 2 giugno. “Libano colpito brutalmente e in modo indebito”. Poi punta il dito contro “le cattive pratiche che raccolgono velocemente adepti”

republika.title: Misterbianco, è morta la donna massacrata di botte dal marito sabato scorso
republika.description: Non ce l’ha fatta la 49enne colpita dall’uomo 53enne. Troppo gravi le lesioni provocate durante una lite nella cittadina alle porte di Catania. A trovare il corpo della madre sul pavimento e a dare l’allarme era stata una delle figlie

republika.title: Valbrembo, Cessna con due persone cade tra le case: morto l’istruttore Daniel Taino, un ferito grave
republika.description: Nella bergamasca: la vittima estratta dalle lamiere. L’aereo, stando a quanto finora ricostruito dai carabinieri, era decollato dall’aviosuperficie di Valbrembo per una lezione

republika.title: Propaganda Isis, 21enne fermato in Brianza: “Pronto al martirio, riferimenti ai fatti di Modena”
republika.description: Accusato di terrorismo internazionale, Zakaria Ben Haddi è al centro di una inchiesta della procura di Milano: “Percorso di indottrinamento e radicalizzazione via web”

republika.title: Cavalli in fuga, i quattro vigili coinvolti saranno esclusi dai servizi operativi
republika.description: Il comandante De Sclavis: “L'esplosione dei fuochi d'artificio che ha fatto imbizzarrire gli animali tra venerdì e sabato è stato un gesto sciocco”

republika.title: Cobolli e Berrettini ai quarti al Roland Garros: battuti Svajda e Cerundolo
republika.description: Flavio rischia grosso nel finale ma centra i quarti in un Major per la seconda volta in carriera. prestazione perfetta di Matteo che chiude in 3 set. Ora in campo Arnaldi-Tiafoe

republika.title: Wenders sulla scena di nudo di Nastassja Kinski: “Avevo 29 anni, non mi posso rimproverare nulla”
republika.description: Il regista interviene sulla richiesta dell’attrice di rimuovere la sequenza del film “Falso Movimento” del 1975

republika.title: Sanremo 2027, la svolta di De Martino: una serata per scegliere il rappresentante all’Eurovision
republika.description: Prime indiscrezioni sul Festival: nuovo regolamento, gara dedicata all’Eurofestival e il possibile ritorno dei big della musica italiana

phys-org.description: Scientists from six Asian countries have launched an ambitious 10-year effort to build synthetic cells from non-living molecules, marking the region's first coordinated push to create an artificial single-celled biological system. phys-org.title: Fast-moving droplets synthesize key drug compounds at room temperature, no catalysts needed
phys-org.description: Chemical reactions are the backbone to nearly all biological processes, including those used to make new medicines. However, these reactions can often take considerable time and require harsh conditions or materials—potentially inhibiting the timely development of life-changing drugs.

phys-org.title: The Y chromosome is home to surprising jumping genes
phys-org.description: The humble Y chromosome may be the smallest chromosome in the mammalian genome (and getting even smaller), but it is mighty: Genes on the Y chromosome are critical for fertility in males. In a new study in the journal Current Biology, researchers at the University of Michigan Medical School have studied deer mice to outline how the Y chromosome defends itself against decay by acquiring gene families, holding its own to maintain fertility.

phys-org.title: Fiber optic components enable high-performance 2-µm fiber lasers
phys-org.description: Laser systems operating in the 2-micrometer wavelength range open diverse opportunities in medical technology, agriculture, and plastics processing. In the Eurostars project DECOMP, Laser Zentrum Hannover e.V. (LZH) has developed novel fiber optic components that overcome previous technical barriers.

phys-org.title: Understanding how things connect helps people invent, 1,200-player experiment suggests
phys-org.description: Our capacity for innovation, rather than being the work of random variation, is based on an intrinsic understanding of how the world works, claim Karolinska Institutet and Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam researchers in a new study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

phys-org.title: Eight metabolic niches reveal how ocean microbes recycle carbon worldwide
phys-org.description: The ocean is full of invisible workers. Trillions of microbes quietly break down carbon-containing organic matter, which helps to regulate Earth's climate. But scientists have long struggled to understand how different microbes contribute to the process.

phys-org.title: COVID-era assistance policies may have reduced food insecurity, housing instability
phys-org.description: In 2018, Caitlin Caspi started a five-year research project looking at how raising the minimum wage could impact nutrition-related health outcomes. Caspi is an associate professor of allied health sciences in the College of Agriculture, Health and Natural Resources (CAHNR), associate director of InCHIP, and the director of food security initiatives for the UConn Rudd Center for Food Policy and Health.

phys-org.title: Microbes turn biodiesel byproduct into three nylon building blocks, opening greener route
phys-org.description: Nylon is a representative plastic material used throughout our daily lives, from clothing to automobiles. However, most of its raw materials have been produced through petrochemical processes, resulting in large carbon emissions. KAIST researchers have developed a technology that can produce key nylon precursors in an eco-friendly way using microbes.

phys-org.title: Low-cost workflow creates 100,000 uniform cell capsules with standard lab tools
phys-org.description: Cells are typically studied outside the body under controlled laboratory conditions. However, conventional flat cell culture methods do not fully reproduce the complex three-dimensional environments that cells experience in living tissues. Tiny hydrogel capsules offer one way to culture cells in a confined three-dimensional space, allowing researchers to study how cells grow, organize and interact under more tissue-like conditions. Current methods to do this come with a high cost and a set of re

phys-org.title: Matter may entangle with light far more easily near quantum critical points
phys-org.description: Quantum entanglement is a state in which particles are entwined with each other. In this entwined state, the properties of one particle influence the other, even when they aren't physically close to each other. This phenomenon has often been observed in small quantum systems with only a few particles in them, where researchers can use it to store and process quantum information. Rice University professor Qimiao Si is interested in understanding and applying quantum entanglement to macroscop

phys-org.title: Cold-grown plankton shells sharpen Arctic climate reconstructions
phys-org.description: Researchers at iC3 have found a way to improve records of past high latitude ocean change using tiny plankton shells called foraminifera. By growing these foraminifera under controlled cold-water conditions, the team has extended a key temperature tool into the range most relevant for subpolar and polar oceans.

phys-org.title: From hybrids to 'virgin birth,' stick insects reveal stepwise loss of sex
phys-org.description: The evolution of sex remains one of biology's greatest puzzles. While sexual reproduction dominates across the animal kingdom, scientists still debate why it persists despite its high costs. Even more mysterious is the loss of sex in favor of asexual reproduction whereby females give birth to copies of themselves without any contribution from males.

phys-org.title: Many more US voters support gay candidates, but only if they look and act 'straight,' study finds
phys-org.description: The period between 2018 and 2022, sometimes referred to as "the rainbow wave," featured an unprecedented increase in LGBTQ candidates elected to office. Pete Buttigieg's rise from mayor of South Bend, Indiana, to U.S. secretary of transportation with a 2020 bid for president in between sparked a national dialogue about whether gay candidates no longer faced an electoral penalty at the ballot box.

phys-org.title: Magnetic field during catalyst synthesis triples ammonia yield
phys-org.description: Applying an external magnetic field during the synthesis of CoFe2O4 electrocatalysts triples the ammonia yield during electrocatalytic conversion. The magnetic field alters the surface states of the spinel oxide thin films, making catalytically active sites more accessible. In the journal Advanced Functional Materials, a team led by Marcel Risch at HZB and Sanjay Mathur at University of Cologne demonstrates a scalable strategy for developing next-generation electrocatalysts for efficient and sus

phys-org.title: 'Molecular movie' technology reveals a better way to thwart environmental pollutant
phys-org.description: The latest production from the "molecular movie" imaging technology developed at Oregon State University is a new, inexpensive way of dealing with a common environmental pollutant. Based on short-pulse lasers, the imaging technology allows chemical and biological actions to be measured as they are occurring, one high-speed frame at a time.

phys-org.title: How a giant moon and a steam atmosphere built the recipe for life
phys-org.description: 4.5 billion years ago was an interesting time for Earth. The atmosphere was thick and what we would now think of as toxic. The moon, which was freshly formed, looks much more massive than it does today and faintly glows with the residual heat from its own creation. And the floor was literally lava. Everywhere. If there were any children alive at the time, they would have no chance of winning that game. But for a long time, scientists had thought this molten phase of Earth didn't last long.

phys-org.title: Wounds may trigger 'aged' cells within hours, reshaping how senescence starts
phys-org.description: What if a process we associate with aging actually helps the body heal? A study led by Mikolaj Ogrodnik, LBI Trauma, published in Nature Cell Biology, shows that cells enter a state of senescence within minutes to hours after an injury—and that this rapid response not only plays a key role in wound healing, but also changes the paradigm of how slowly senescence was expected to arise.

phys-org.title: Innovative local collaboration can unlock stronger environmental protection in England, study shows
phys-org.description: The use of digital tools and better coordination between different organizations can help the U.K. significantly optimize its first line of defense against ecological degradation, new research shows. Unified and local efforts can support a thriving environment and improve community well-being, University of Exeter experts have found. They hope their blueprint—which proposes tech-driven, community-led action—can rescue local environmental enforcement from funding cuts and jurisdictional confusion

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

undark.title: Book Review: The Life and Struggles of a Conservation Pioneer
undark.description: Over a career of many decades, George Schaller laid the groundwork for the field of conservation biology, and his pioneering research likely saved numerous species from extinction. In “Homesick for a World Unknown,” Miriam Horn documents his triumphs, challenges, and setbacks in meticulous detail.

undark.title: Medicine’s Move Toward Race-Neutral Risk Assessments
undark.description: Earlier this year, new guidelines were released for doctors assessing a patient’s risk for heart disease. The guidelines take a race-neutral and patient-informed approach that’s rooted in up-to-date science, one doctor writes, and offer a glimpse of a future in which health equity is the standard in medicine.

undark.title: In Coal Country, Black Lung Surges as Federal Protections Stall
undark.description: While the Trump administration is directing hundreds of millions of dollars to coal projects, miners in Appalachia are suffering from a resurgence of black lung disease. But industry pushback is delaying federal rules that would reduce miners’ exposure to deadly silica dust.

proj-syn.title: The One Man Who Could Give Trump Middle East Peace
proj-syn.description: With a large majority of UN member states recognizing Palestine on the 1967 lines, there is a clear international blueprint for creating an independent Palestinian state alongside Israel. What has been missing is credible Palestinian leadership of the kind that the imprisoned politician Marwan Barghouti could provide.

proj-syn.title: Europe’s Nuclear Options
proj-syn.description: The risks raised by nuclear weapons remain as potent as ever, but the institutional framework that mitigated them has been severely eroded. The task now is to prevent deterrence from giving way to proliferation—which, for Europe, means building conventional capabilities, keeping the US engaged, and upholding restraint.

proj-syn.title: The Intelligence That AI Is Missing
proj-syn.description: For AI to simplify humans’ complex social and professional lives, it cannot just give tidy answers based on whatever the internet has to say about our values. It will need the capacity to account for our relational commitments, which are typically grounded in personal identity, experience, and culture.

proj-syn.title: Why Isn’t Europe Poorer Than the US?
proj-syn.description: Nobel laureate Paul Krugman has a point when he says that European living standards have largely kept pace with those in the US, despite flagging growth and innovation. But this will not remain true indefinitely: restoring Europe's ability to compete at the technological frontier remains essential to its future well-being.

proj-syn.title: The Real Choice Confronting Developing Countries
proj-syn.description: Lost in the debate about whether developing countries should pursue manufacturing- or services-led growth is the potential for new AI tools to make even informal workers far more productive. If governments can broaden access to such technologies, they no longer need to choose between strategies.

proj-syn.title: India’s Great Political Realignment
proj-syn.description: In recent years, the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party’s focus on religious identity, together with its “purification” of voter rolls, has created a more binary—and potentially volatile—political landscape, where elections increasingly reflect ethno-religious identity. This month’s elections in five states largely confirmed this trend.

proj-syn.title: Central Banking in an Age of Global Supply Shocks
proj-syn.description: The core assumptions underlying the decades-old inflation-targeting orthodoxy have proven to be unfit for a geopolitically fragmented world characterized by frequent supply-side disruptions. Under such conditions, central banks' traditional monetary policies are only as effective as markets believe them to be.

proj-syn.title: The Tech-MAGA Breakup Is Coming
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump has managed to fuse a backward-looking populist movement with a Silicon Valley vanguard whose guiding assumption is that AI will render a large share of ordinary people economically redundant. But with the tech billionaires now rewiring America's electricity grid and driving up costs, a split seems inevitable.

proj-syn.title: A Professor Should Work Hard and Grade Easy
proj-syn.description: The Harvard University faculty has now decided to limit the share of “A” grades given to students to about 20%. But, as the move's defenders freely admit, the intent is to increase professors' power and students' stress, not to generate excitement in the classroom.

proj-syn.title: What Price Hormuz?
proj-syn.description: Donald Trump has three primary objectives in the Persian Gulf: unwind the Iranian nuclear program, permanently reopen the Strait of Hormuz, and not be the president blamed for having “lost” Taiwan to China. The bad news for the US president is that he can achieve at most two of these goals.

proj-syn.title: The Mismeasurement of Europe’s Productivity
proj-syn.description: The Nobel laureate economist Paul Krugman uses the wrong metric—purchasing power parity—to make the case that Europe is not lagging far behind the US in terms of productivity. The right metric shows that the gap is growing.

proj-syn.title: Latin America’s Agricultural Boom Is Faltering

proj-syn.title: Americans Can’t Afford Trump’s Economy

proj-syn.title: Britain’s Center Cannot Hold
proj-syn.description: A combination of globalization, deindustrialization, and other forces destroyed the old model of party politics that long prevailed in developed democracies. Nowhere is this more apparent than in the United Kingdom, where voters are angry and demanding radical solutions that no political leader can actually deliver.

proj-syn.title: Reading Between China’s Red Lines
proj-syn.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping’s blunt warning to US President Donald Trump about Taiwan was clearly intended to sharpen the distinction between this ultimatum and the many others Xi has issued. proj-syn.title: The Pope Should Have Gone Further on AI

proj-syn.title: China’s Long March to Technological Supremacy

proj-syn.title: The Pope’s Defense of Humanity
proj-syn.description: Pope Leo XIV is right to celebrate the grandeur of humanity, to criticize and reject posthumanism, and to emphasize the essential, categorical, and insurmountable difference between humans and machines. His first encyclical is a necessary exhortation to believers and non-believers alike.
